chapter: Left out of the jazz books; Tatum, Handy and family
title: Harlem after-hours with Tatum: Marlowe Morris and the piano players at Rubens
summary: Between sets at Cafe Society, Tatum visited the Hollywood Club and Rubens, where Teddy Wilson and others played first and then Tatum wiped everyone out.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Art Tatum: the legend, the piano and the man

blocks.x: But any way, Art loved piano players, as you know, and we were working together, another time, in New York at Cafe

Society downtown. And during the intermission we would drive uptown, say we had a bottle, and had two hours off. We would drive uptown to a little club of a friend of his, Tom Tillman, who owned this club, the Hollywood Club, and we would go up here to listen to the beetle -- these are stride piano players.

Or whoever was there. What was this guy's name? Marlowe Morris. Was a great stride piano player. So we would go up here between shows, and we'd have the chauffeur to drive us back down to finish. After that he would -- we would go to another place -- when we finished work rather we would go to another club called Rubens. Now, you understand that I was always with him. Okay. We would go to Rubins.

Now, this is a place we -- you go in the building and you go down a flight of stairs to the basement, and you go through a tunnel to another building, and then a little room. I think the floor plan -- say like a 9 by 12 rug, you get in there. There's Teddy Wilson, Chittison, Herman Chittison, just all of the piano players waiting for Art.

This was in Harlem. This was in Harlem, I forget, it was around 132 or somewhere around there. But this -- I remember this place, it was called Rubens. And we would go in here and they would all play. And when they finished, Art would wipe everybody out. Just -- and then in

the meantime he's drinking beer, always drinking this beer, you know. At one time he just used to drink quite a bit of whiskey but I think towards the last he was just drinking beer. But he was there drinking until everybody finished and he loved everybody's playing, you know, but then came the thunder, you know. It was just beautiful. This is what they were waiting for. They wanted to hurry up and get through so they could hear him play. They knew he would not play until they had finished. And he would just play for hours.
